2:2: That is the Book in which there is no doubt, a guidance for the muttaqin.
2:3: They believe in the unseen, perform the salah properly, and spend from what We have provided them as provision.
2:4: And they believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, and they firmly believe in the Hereafter as well.
2:5: Those are upon guidance from their Rabb, and those are the very ones who attain salvation.
2:6: Indeed, whether you warn those who disbelieve or do not warn them, it is the same for them; they do not believe.
2:7: Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil, and for them is a great punishment.
2:8: And among the people are those who say, 'We have believed in Allah and the Last Day,' but they are not believers.
2:9: They deceive Allah and those who believe, yet they deceive none but themselves, and they do not realize.
2:10: In their hearts is a disease, so Allah has increased their disease; and for them is a painful punishment because they have been lying.
2:11: And when it is said to them, 'Do not cause corruption on the earth,' they say, 'We are only reformers.'
2:12: Beware, indeed they are the very corrupters, but they do not realize.
2:13: And when it is said to them, 'Believe as the people have believed,' they say, 'Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?' Know that indeed, they are the foolish, but they do not know.
2:14: And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We have believed'; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, 'Indeed, we are with you, and we were only mocking.'
2:15: Allah mocks them and leaves them wandering blindly in their transgression.
2:16: Those are the ones who bought astrayness in exchange for guidance, so their commerce did not profit, nor did they find the right way.
2:17: Their condition is like the condition of the one who kindled a fire; when it illuminated around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses, they do not see.
2:18: They are deaf, dumb, and blind; therefore they do not return.
2:19: Or like a rainstorm from the sky, in which are darknesses, thunder, and lightning; they thrust their fingers into their ears against the thunderbolts out of fear of death, and Allah encompasses the disbelievers.
2:20: The lightning almost takes away their sight; whenever it gives them light, they walk in it, and whenever darkness falls upon them, they stand still. If Allah had willed, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is powerful over all things.
2:21: O people! Worship your Rabb who created you and those before you, that you may guard yourselves.
2:22: He who made the earth a resting place for you and the sky a canopy, and sent down water from the sky and brought forth fruits with it as provision for you. So do not set up equals to Allah knowingly.
2:23: And if you are in doubt concerning what We have sent down to Our servant, then produce a surah like it and call your witnesses besides Allah, if you are truthful.
2:24: If you do not—and you will never be able to—then guard against the Fire whose fuel is men and stones, which has been prepared for the disbelievers.
2:25: And give glad tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds; indeed, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with any fruit from them as provision, they say, 'This is what we were provided with before.' And they are brought something similar to it. For them there are purified spouses therein, and they will abide therein eternally.
2:26: Indeed, Allah does not shy away from giving an example of a mosquito or what is above it. As for those who believe, they know that it is the truth from their Rabb. As for those who disbelieve, they say, 'What did Allah intend by this example?' Allah misguides many with it, and guides many with it. And He misguides none with it except the fasiqun.
2:27: Those who break the covenant of Allah after ratifying it, cut what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on the earth. Those are the losers.
2:28: How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He brought you to life? Then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life again, and then to Him you will be returned.
2:29: He is the One who created for you everything on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven and fashioned them as seven heavens. And He is the Knower of all things.
2:30: And when your Rabb said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will create a khalifah on the earth.' They said, 'Will You create someone in it who will cause corruption in it and shed blood? While we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You.' Allah said, 'Indeed, I know what you do not know.'
2:31: And He taught Adam all the names. Then He showed them to the angels and said, 'Tell me the names of these, if you are truthful.'
2:32: They said, 'Exalted are You! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us; indeed You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.'
2:33: He said, 'O Adam, inform them of their names.' When he informed them of their names, He said, 'Did I not say to you, indeed I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you disclose and what you have been concealing?'
2:34: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate before Adam.' They all prostrated, except Iblis. He resisted, was arrogant, and became of the disbelievers.
2:35: And We said, 'O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden and eat freely from it wherever you wish, and do not approach this tree, lest you become of the wrongdoers.'
2:36: Thereupon, Satan made them slip from it and brought them out of where they had been. And We said, 'Get down, enemies to one another.'
2:37: Thereupon, Adam received words from his Rabb, so his Rabb accepted his repentance. Indeed, He is the One who accepts repentance, the Most Merciful.
2:38: We said, 'Get down from it, all of you. Whenever guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.'
2:39: And those who disbelieve and deny Our verses are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
2:40: O Children of Israel, remember My favor that I bestowed upon you, and fulfill My covenant so that I may fulfill your covenant, and fear Me alone.
2:41: Believe in what I have sent down, confirming what is with you, and do not be the first to disbelieve in it, and do not sell My verses for a small price, and fear Me alone.
2:42: And do not mix the truth with falsehood, and do not conceal the truth while you know.
2:43: And establish salah, give zakat, and bow down with those who bow down.
2:44: Do you enjoin righteousness upon people and forget yourselves, while you recite the Book? Will you not use your intellect?
2:45: Seek help through patience and salah, and surely it is indeed great except to those who feel reverence.
2:46: They are those who think that they will meet their Rabb and that they will return to Him.
2:47: O Children of Israel! Remember My favor that I bestowed upon you and that I made you superior over the worlds.
2:48: And beware of a day when no soul shall pay anything on behalf of another soul, nor shall intercession be accepted from it, nor shall ransom be taken from it, and they shall not be helped.
2:49: And when We had saved you from the family of Pharaoh; they were afflicting you with the worst of punishment, slaughtering your sons and letting your women live, and in that was a great trial from your Rabb.
2:50: And when We parted the sea for you, We saved you and drowned the family of Pharaoh while you were looking on.
2:51: And when We appointed for Moses forty nights, then you took the calf after him, acting unjustly.
2:52: Then after that We forgave you so that you might be grateful.
2:53: And when We gave Moses the Book and the Furqan, so that you might find guidance.
2:54: And when Moses said to his people: "O my people, surely you have wronged your souls by taking the calf. So repent to your Rabb Who is Maker (al-Bari) and kill your souls. This is better for you in the sight of your Rabb Who is Maker." Thus He turned toward you in repentance. Surely He is the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful.
2:55: And when you said: "O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah openly." Thereupon the thunderbolt struck you while you were looking on.
2:56: Then after your death We revived you so that you might be grateful.
2:57: And We made the cloud shade over you and sent down upon you manna and quails. We said: Eat of the pure things We have provided for you.
2:58: And when We said: Enter this town and eat bountifully from it wherever you wish, and enter the gate prostrating and say 'forgive'; We will forgive your mistakes, and We will increase even more for the doers of good.
2:59: Those who did wrong changed the word that was said to them into another word; thereupon We sent down upon those who did wrong a punishment from heaven because they were acting defiantly.
2:60: When Moses asked for water for his people, We said, 'Strike the stone with your staff!' Twelve springs gushed forth from it. Everyone knew their drinking place. Eat and drink of the provision of Allah, and do not make mischief on the earth, causing corruption.
2:61: And you had said: O Moses, we can never endure a single food, so pray to your Rabb for us that He may bring forth for us of what the earth grows, of its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions. He said: Do you exchange what is better for what is lower? Go down to a city, for you shall have what you asked for. And humiliation and misery were stamped upon them, and they incurred wrath from Allah. That was because they were disbelieving in the verses of Allah and killing the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing.
2:62: Surely those who believe, and those among the Jews, the Christians, and the Sabians who believe in Allah and the Last Day and do righteous deeds, their reward is with their Rabb. There shall be no fear upon them, nor shall they grieve.
2:63: We had taken a firm covenant from you and raised the Mount (Tur) above you. Hold firmly to what We have given you and remember what is in it so that you may beware.
2:64: Then after that you turned away. If it were not for the grace and mercy of Allah upon you, you would certainly have been among the losers.
2:65: And indeed you knew those among you who transgressed concerning the Sabbath, but We said to them: Be disgraced apes.
2:66: We made this an exemplary punishment for those before it and those after it, and an admonition for the people of taqwa.
2:67: And when Moses said to his people: "Surely Allah commands you to slaughter a cow." They said: "Are you taking us in mockery?" He said: "I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant."
2:68: They said: "Pray to your Rabb for us to clarify for us what it is." He said: "Surely He says: It is a cow neither old nor young, middle-aged between the two. So do what you are commanded."
2:69: They said: 'Pray to your Rabb for us to clarify for us what its color is.' He said: 'He says, it is a yellow cow, bright in color, pleasing to onlookers.'
2:70: They said: Pray to your Rabb for us to clarify for us what it is. For the cattle seem similar to us. And we, if Allah wills, are surely the rightly guided.
2:71: He said: 'He says, it is a cow not trained to till the soil nor water the crops, sound, with no blemish in it.' They said: 'Now you have brought the truth.' Then they slaughtered it, and they almost did not do it.
2:72: And when you killed a soul, you disputed concerning it, and Allah is the One Who brings forth what you were concealing.
2:73: Thereupon We said: 'Strike it with a part of it.' Thus Allah brings the dead to life and shows you His signs so that you may reason.
2:74: Then after that your hearts hardened, like stone, or even harder. For indeed of the stones there are some from which rivers gush forth. And of them there are some that split open and water comes out of them. And of them there are some that fall down from the fear of Allah. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
2:75: Do you now hope that they will believe you? Yet a party of them hear the word of Allah, then alter it knowingly after having understood it.
2:76: And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We have believed,' but when they are alone with one another, they say, 'Do you speak to them of what Allah has disclosed to you so that they may argue with you about it before your Rabb? Will you not reason?'
2:77: Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare?
2:78: And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book, except wishful thoughts, and they only speculate.
2:79: Woe to those who write the book with their hands then say, 'This is from Allah,' in order to sell it for a small price. Woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn.
2:80: They said: 'The Fire will never touch us except for a numbered few days.' Say: 'Have you taken a covenant from Allah? Then Allah will not break His promise.
2:81: Yes, whoever earns evil and his sin encompasses him, those are the companions of the fire; they will abide therein eternally.
2:82: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
2:83: And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel: 'Do not serve anyone other than Allah, do good to parents, relatives, orphans, and the poor, speak good words to people, establish salah, and give zakat.' Then, except for a few of you, you turned away, and you are those who turn back.
2:84: And when We took a covenant from you: 'Do not shed your blood and do not expel yourselves from your homelands.' Then you confirmed, and you bear witness.
2:85: Then you, there you are, killing one another and expelling a group among you from their homelands, cooperating against them in sin and hostility. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, whereas expelling them was forbidden to you. Do you then believe in a part of the Book and disbelieve in a part? What is the penalty for whoever does this among you except disgrace in the life of this world? And on the Day of Resurrection, they will be returned to the severest punishment. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
2:86: Those are the ones who bought the life of this world in exchange for the Hereafter; therefore, the punishment will not be lightened for them, and they will not be helped.
2:87: And indeed, We gave Moses the Book and sent messengers successively after him. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit. Is it that whenever a messenger brought you what your souls did not desire, you grew arrogant? A part you denied, and a part you kill.
2:88: And they said: 'Our hearts are covered.' No, rather Allah has cursed them because of their disbelief. Therefore, only a few of them believe.
2:89: And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what is with them – though they previously used to seek victory against those who disbelieved – yet when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it. The curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.
2:90: How evil is that for which they sold their souls; because of their disbelieving, out of insolence, in what Allah sent down of His bounty upon whomever He wills of His servants. Thereupon they incurred wrath upon wrath. And for the disbelievers there is a humiliating punishment.
2:91: And when it is said to them, 'Believe in what Allah has sent down,' they said, 'We believe in what was sent down to us,' and they disbelieve in what is beyond it. Whereas it is the truth, confirming what is with them. Say: 'Then why were you killing Allah's prophets before, if you were believers?'
2:92: And indeed, Moses came to you with clear proofs. Then, after him, you took the calf, and you were wrongdoers.
2:93: And when We took a covenant from you and raised the Mount over you: "Hold what We gave you with strength and listen." They said: "We heard and we disobeyed." And because of their disbelief, the calf was made to drink into their hearts. Say: "How evil is that which your faith commands you, if you are believers."
2:94: Say: If the home of the Hereafter with Allah is exclusively for you to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death if you are truthful.
2:95: They will never wish for it because of what their hands have sent ahead. And Allah is the Knower of the wrongdoers.
2:96: And you will surely find them the greediest of people for life, even greedier than those who associate partners with Allah. Each one of them wishes to be given a life of a thousand years. Yet being granted life will not remove him from the punishment. And Allah is the Seer of what they do.
2:97: Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, then indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by Allah's permission, confirming what was before it, and as guidance and good news for the believers.
2:98: Whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels, His messengers, Gabriel, and Michael, then indeed Allah is the enemy of the disbelievers.
2:99: And indeed, We have sent down to you clear verses. None disbelieve in them except the fasiqun.
2:100: Whenever they made a covenant, did not a group of them break it? No, rather most of them do not believe.
2:101: And when a messenger came to them from Allah, confirming what was with them, a group of those who were given the Book threw the Book of Allah behind their backs.
2:102: And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved; they were teaching people sorcery and what was sent down in Babylon to the two angels, Harut and Marut. But the two did not teach anyone until they said, 'We are only a fitnah, so do not disbelieve.' Thus they learned from them that by which they separate a man and his wife. And they were not harmful to anyone with it except by Allah's permission. They learned what harmed them and did not benefit them. And indeed, they knew that whoever purchased it had no share in the Hereafter. How evil was that for which they sold themselves with it! If only they had known.
2:103: And if they had believed and been mindful, surely a reward from Allah would have been better, if only they had known.
2:104: O you who believe, do not say 'Raina', say 'Unzurna' and listen. And for the disbelievers there is a painful punishment.
2:105: Those who disbelieve among the People of the Book and the polytheists do not wish that any good should be sent down to you from your Rabb, and Allah singles out for His mercy whomever He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
2:106: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring better than it or the like of it. Do you not know that Allah is capable of all things?
2:107: Do you not know that the dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and for you, besides Allah, there is neither a protector nor a helper?
2:108: Or do you wish to question your messenger as Moses was questioned before? And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the straight path.
2:109: Many of the People of the Book wish to turn you back as disbelievers after your faith, out of jealousy in their souls, after the truth has become clear to them. So pardon and overlook, until Allah comes with His command. Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.
2:110: Establish salah and give zakat. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah is the Seer of what you do.
2:111: They said: "None will ever enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." That is their wishful thinking. Say: "Bring your proof if you are truthful."
2:112: Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah and is a doer of good, then his reward is with his Rabb, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
2:113: The Jews said: 'The Christians are not upon anything.' And the Christians said: 'The Jews are not upon anything.' Whereas they read the Book. Those who do not know also said the like of their word. Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which they differed.
2:114: Who is more unjust than one who prevents Allah's name from being mentioned in His masjids and strives for their destruction? Those, they can enter them only fearing. For them in this world is a disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
2:115: Both the east and the west belong to Allah. Whichever way you turn, the face of Allah is there. Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
2:116: They said: "Allah has taken a child." He is transcendent. On the contrary, whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. All are submissive to Him.
2:117: The Originator of the heavens and the earth, and when He decrees a matter, He only says to it 'Be', and it is.
2:118: Those who do not know said: "If only Allah would speak to us or a sign would come to us." Those before them also said the like of their word. Their hearts resembled one another. We have certainly made the signs clear for a people who believe with certainty.
2:119: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bearer of good tidings and a warner, and you will not be asked about the companions of Hell.
2:120: The Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with you until you follow their religion. Say: 'Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the true guidance itself.' By oath, if you follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, there is for you from Allah neither a protector nor a helper.
2:121: Those to whom We gave the Book read it with its true reading. Those, they believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers.
2:122: O Children of Israel! Remember My blessing which I bestowed upon you, and that I favored you above the worlds.
2:123: And guard yourselves against a day when no soul will pay anything on behalf of another soul, no ransom will be accepted from it, and intercession will not benefit them.
2:124: And when his Rabb tested Abraham with certain words, and he fulfilled them. Allah said: 'I will make you an imam for the people.' Abraham said: 'And from my offspring too?' Allah said: 'My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.'
2:125: And when We made the House a place of gathering and security for the people. Take a place of prayer from the station of Abraham. And We covenanted with Abraham and Ishmael: 'Purify My House for those who perform tawaf, those who stay (for worship), and those who bow down, those who prostrate.'
2:126: And when Abraham said: 'My Rabb, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits—those among them who believe in Allah and the Last Day.' He said: 'And whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little while, then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire; and what an evil destination it is.'
2:127: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, they said: 'Our Rabb, accept from us, indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.'
2:128: Our Rabb! Make us both submissive to You, and from our lineage a nation submissive to You; and show us our ways of worship and accept our repentance. Indeed You are the One Who accepts repentance repeatedly, the Merciful.
2:129: Our Rabb, send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them.
2:130: And who turns away from the religion of Abraham except one who fools himself? By oath, We chose him in the world, and indeed in the Hereafter he is among the righteous.
2:131: When his Rabb said to him, 'Submit,' he said, 'I have submitted to the Rabb of the worlds.'
2:132: Abraham enjoined this upon his sons, and Jacob too, saying: 'O my sons! Indeed, Allah has chosen for you the religion, so do not die except as Muslims.'
2:133: Or were you witnesses when death came to Jacob? When he said to his sons: 'What will you worship after me?' They said: 'We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, one single God, and to Him we are submissive.'
2:134: That is a nation that has passed away. For it is what it earned, and for you is what you earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.
2:135: They said: 'Be Jews or Christians so that you may find the right path.' Say: 'No, rather the religion of Abraham, as a hanif. And he was not of the polytheists.'
2:136: Say: 'We have believed in Allah, and in what was revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the descendants, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what was given to the prophets from their Rabb. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we are submissive.'
2:137: If they believe as you have believed, they have truly attained guidance; and if they turn away, then they are only in dissension, and soon Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
2:138: The dye of Allah, and who has a better dye than Allah? And we are worshippers of Him.
2:139: Say: 'Do you dispute with us about Allah, while He is our Rabb and your Rabb? Our deeds belong to us and your deeds belong to you, and we are sincerely devoted to Him.'
2:140: Or do you say that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the descendants were Jews or Christians? Say: 'Do you know better, or does Allah?' And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony that is with him from Allah? Allah is not unaware of what you do.
2:141: That is a nation that has passed away. For it is what it earned, and for you is what you earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.
2:142: The foolish among the people will say: 'What has turned them away from their qiblah which they were upon?' Say: 'Both the east and the west belong to Allah. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.'
2:143: And thus We have made you a middle nation so that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you. And We made the qiblah which you were upon only that We might distinguish the one who follows the Messenger from the one who turns back on his heels. And indeed, this was certainly a great burden, except for those whom Allah has guided. And Allah would never cause your faith to be lost. Indeed, Allah is certainly full of kindness, Most Merciful toward people.
2:144: We certainly see the turning of your face in the sky. We will certainly turn you toward a qiblah that you will be pleased with. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you may be, turn your faces toward it. And indeed, those who were given the Book certainly know that it is the truth from their Rabb. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.
2:145: By oath, if you were to bring every kind of sign to those who were given the Scripture, they would not follow your qiblah; nor do you follow their qiblah; nor does a part of them follow the qiblah of another. By oath, if you follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, then indeed you would truly be among the wrongdoers.
2:146: Those to whom We gave the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their own sons, and undoubtedly a group of them surely conceals the truth.
2:147: The truth is from your Rabb, so do not be among the doubters.
2:148: Everyone has a direction to which he turns. Race in good deeds. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together. Undoubtedly, Allah is capable of all things.
2:149: From wherever you set out, turn your face toward the direction of al-Masjid al-Haram; and undoubtedly it is a truth from your Rabb, and Allah is not heedless of what you do.
2:150: From wherever you set out, turn your face toward the side of al-Masjid al-Haram. Wherever you may be, turn your faces toward that direction so that there will be no argument for the people against you, except those among them who do wrong. Do not fear them, fear Me. And it is so that I may complete My blessing upon you and that you may find the right way.
2:151: Just as We sent to you a messenger from among you, reciting to you Our signs, purifying you, teaching you the Scripture and wisdom, and teaching you what you did not know.
2:152: So remember Me, that I may remember you; and be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful.
2:153: O you who believe, seek help through patience and salah. Undoubtedly, Allah is with the patient.
2:154: Do not say 'dead' to those who are killed in the way of Allah; rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive.
2:155: By oath, We test you with a little fear, a little hunger, and a decrease in wealth, lives, and crops; and give glad tidings to the patient.
2:156: Those who, whenever a misfortune strikes them, say: 'Undoubtedly we belong to Allah, and undoubtedly to Him we are returning.'
2:157: Those, upon them are blessings of forgiveness and mercy from their Rabb, and those, they are the rightly guided.
2:158: Undoubtedly, Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. Whoever performs Hajj to the House or performs Umrah, there is no sin upon him in walking between them. And whoever does good voluntarily, undoubtedly Allah is Appreciative, Knowing.
2:159: As for those who conceal the clear proofs and the guidance We have sent down after We have explained it to the people in the Scripture, it is they whom Allah curses, and the cursers curse them as well.
2:160: Except those who repent, make amends, and make clear. Those, I accept their repentance. I am the One Who accepts repentance much, the exceedingly Merciful.
2:161: Undoubtedly, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, upon them is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all the people.
2:162: They are eternal abiders therein; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
2:163: Your deity is one deity. There is no deity except Him. He is al-Rahman, al-Rahim.
2:164: Undoubtedly, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of night and day, the ships that sail in the sea with what benefits people, Allah sending down water from the sky and reviving the earth therewith after its death and dispersing therein every kind of living creature, and in the turning of the winds and the clouds subjected between heaven and earth, there are surely signs for a people who reflect.
2:165: And among the people are some who take equals besides Allah, loving them as they love Allah; but those who believe are stronger in love for Allah. And if only those who do wrong would see, when they see the punishment, that power belongs entirely to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment!
2:166: At that time, those who were followed will disown those who followed, they will see the punishment, and all ties between them will be severed.
2:167: Those who followed will say: 'If only there were a return for us, so that we might disown them as they have disowned us.' Thus Allah shows them their deeds as regrets. And they are not to come out of the Fire.
2:168: O people! Eat of what is lawful and good on the earth, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Undoubtedly, he is an open enemy to you.
2:169: He only commands you to evil and immorality, and that you say concerning Allah that which you do not know.
2:170: When it is said to them, 'Follow what Allah has sent down,' they say, 'No, we follow that upon which we found our fathers.' What if their fathers did not reason anything and did not find the right way?
2:171: The state of those who disbelieve is like the state of one who shouts to that which hears nothing except a call and a cry. Deaf, mute, blind; therefore they do not reason.
2:172: O you who believe, eat from the good things of what We have provided you, and be grateful to Allah if it is only Him you worship.
2:173: He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which is slaughtered in the name of other than Allah. But whoever is forced by necessity, without transgressing or acting with hostility, there is no sin upon him. Undoubtedly, Allah is much forgiving, very merciful.
2:174: Undoubtedly, those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Scripture and exchange it for a small value, they eat nothing into their bellies except fire. Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment.
2:175: Those are the ones who have bought error in exchange for guidance, and punishment in exchange for forgiveness. How patient He has made them against the Fire!
2:176: This is because Allah sent down the Scripture with truth, and undoubtedly those who differ concerning the Scripture are in a distant separation.
2:177: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east and west. But righteousness is [that of] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Scripture, and the prophets; and gives wealth, despite love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, beggars, and for freeing slaves; and performs salah, gives zakat; those who fulfill their covenants (when they make a covenant), and those who are patient in hardship, illness, and at the time of battle. Those are the ones who are truthful, and those are the possessors of taqwa.
2:178: O you who believe, qisas is prescribed for you regarding those who are killed: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female. But whoever is pardoned anything by his brother, then there is following according to custom and paying to him with goodness. This is an alleviation and mercy from your Rabb. And whoever commits aggression after this, for him is a painful punishment.
2:179: O possessors of intellect! In qisas there is life for you, so that you may beware.
2:180: When death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind good, bequest with goodness to parents and relatives has been prescribed for you. This is a duty upon the possessors of taqwa.
2:181: Whoever alters it after hearing it, its sin is upon those who alter it. Surely Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
2:182: Whoever fears an error or sin from a testator and reconciles between them, there is no sin upon him. Surely Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
2:183: O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you so that you may guard yourselves.
2:184: Counted days. Whoever among you is ill or on a journey, completes the number from other days. For those who are capable of it, there is a ransom: feeding a poor person. Whoever does good voluntarily, that is better for him. And that you fast is better for you, if you know.
2:185: The month of Ramadan, in which the Quran was sent down; as guidance for mankind, clear proofs from guidance, and the criterion between right and wrong. Whichever of you witnesses this month, let him fast it. Whoever is ill or on a journey, keeps count from other days. Allah desires ease for you, He does not desire hardship for you; so that you may complete the count and glorify Allah for guiding you, and so that you may give thanks.
2:186: And when My servants ask you about Me, surely I am near. I answer the call of the caller when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me so that they may attain the right path.
2:187: Approaching your women on the night of fasting has been made lawful for you. They are a garment for you, and you are a garment for them. Allah knew that you were betraying yourselves, so He accepted your repentance and forgave you. Now approach them and seek what Allah has written for you. And eat and drink until the white thread is distinguished from the black thread at dawn. Then complete the fast until night. And do not approach them while you are in itikaf in the mosques. These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them. Thus Allah makes clear His signs to people that they may guard themselves.
2:188: Do not consume your wealth among yourselves in vanity, and do not convey it to judges knowingly in order to consume a portion of the wealth of people in sin.
2:189: They ask you about the crescents. Say: They are time measurements for people and the hajj. Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is of the one who has taqwa. Enter houses from their doors. Guard against Allah so that you may attain salvation.
2:190: Fight in the way of Allah with those who fight you, and do not transgress. Surely Allah does not love the transgressors.
2:191: Kill them wherever you find them, and expel them from where they expelled you. Fitnah is more severe than killing. Do not fight them beside al-Masjid al-Haram unless they fight you there. If they fight you, kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.
2:192: If they cease, then surely Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
2:193: Fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is only for Allah. If they cease, then there is no hostility except against the wrongdoers.
2:194: The sacred month is for the sacred month, and the sacred things are subject to retaliation. Whoever attacks you, retaliate against him in the same way he attacked you. Fear Allah and know that Allah is with those who have taqwa.
2:195: Spend in the way of Allah and do not throw yourselves into danger with your own hands, and do good. Surely Allah loves those who do good.
2:196: Complete the hajj and umrah for Allah. If you are detained, send whatever sacrifice is easy for you, and do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination. Whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of his head, a ransom from fasting or charity or sacrifice is required. When you are secure, whoever benefits from umrah until hajj shall slaughter whatever sacrifice is easy for him. Whoever cannot find one shall fast three days during hajj and seven days when you return; that is ten complete days. This is for those whose family is not present at al-Masjid al-Haram. Guard against Allah and know that Allah's punishment is very severe.
2:197: Hajj is in the well-known months. Whoever makes hajj obligatory upon himself in those months, there is no sexual intimacy, no wickedness, and no disputing during hajj. Whatever good you do, Allah knows it. Take provision, surely the best provision is taqwa. O people of understanding, guard against Me.
2:198: There is no sin upon you in seeking bounty from your Rabb. When you surge from Arafat, remember Allah beside al-Mash'ar al-Haram. And remember Him as He has guided you. Indeed, before that you were among those who were astray.
2:199: Then surge from where the people surge and ask forgiveness from Allah, surely Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
2:200: When you have completed your acts of worship, remember Allah as you remember your fathers or with an even greater remembrance. Among people there are those who say: "Our Rabb, give to us in this world." And there is no share for him in the Hereafter.
2:201: And among them are those who say: "Our Rabb, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."
2:202: Those, for them is a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning.
2:203: Remember Allah during the counted days. Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him either. This is for whoever guards against evil. Guard against Allah and know that you will be gathered unto Him.
2:204: And of mankind there is he whose speech in the worldly life astonishes you, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of adversaries.
2:205: When he turns away, he strives throughout the earth to cause corruption therein and to destroy crops and progeny. Allah does not love corruption.
2:206: When it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride drives him into sin; so Hell is sufficient for him, and what an evil resting place it is.
2:207: And of mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. Allah is very compassionate to His servants.
2:208: O you who believe, enter into peace all together and do not follow the footsteps of Satan, for indeed he is a clear enemy to you.
2:209: If you slip after clear proofs have come to you, know that surely Allah is All-Mighty, Possessor of judgment and wisdom.
2:210: Do they wait for Allah to come to them in the shadows of clouds and with the angels? Whereas the matter has already been decreed.
2:211: Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them; whoever changes the blessing of Allah after it has come to him, then surely Allah is very severe in punishment.
2:212: The life of this world is beautified for those who disbelieve, and they ridicule those who believe. Those who have taqwa will be above them on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah provides for whom He wills without measure.
2:213: Mankind was a single community. Then Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners. And He sent down with them the Book with truth, to judge between the people concerning the matters in which they differed. And none differed in it except those who differed out of transgression among themselves after clear proofs had come to them. Then Allah guided those who believed, by His permission, to the truth concerning which they had differed. Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
2:214: Or did you think that you would enter Paradise, while the likeness of those who passed before you has not yet come to you? Severe distress and affliction touched them, and they were shaken, so that the messenger and those who believed with him said, 'When is the help of Allah?' Beware, surely the help of Allah is near.
2:215: They ask you what they should spend. Say: 'Whatever you spend of good, (it) belongs to parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, and the traveler. And whatever you do of good, surely Allah is Knower of it.'
2:216: Fighting is ordained for you, though it is something you dislike. It may be that you dislike something and it is good for you, and it may be that you love something and it is bad for you. Allah knows, and you do not know.
2:217: They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say: 'Fighting in it is a great sin. But hindering from the way of Allah, disbelief in Him, preventing from al-Masjid al-Haram, and driving its people out from there is greater in the sight of Allah.' Fitnah is greater than killing. If they are able, they will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion. And whoever among you turns back from his religion and dies as a disbeliever, then those—their deeds have come to nothing in this world and the Hereafter. Those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally.
2:218: Surely those who believe, and those who emigrate and strive in the way of Allah, it is they who hope for the mercy of Allah. Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
2:219: They ask you about intoxicants and gambling. Say: 'In both of them is a great sin and benefits for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit.' And they ask you what they should spend. Say: 'The surplus.' Thus does Allah make clear the verses to you, so that you may reflect.
2:220: Concerning this world and the Hereafter. They ask you about orphans. Say: 'To set right their affairs is good. And if you mix with them, they are your brothers. Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer. And had Allah willed, He would have put you in hardship. Surely Allah is al-Aziz, al-Hakim.'
2:221: Do not marry polytheist women until they believe. A believing bondwoman is better than a polytheist woman, even if she pleases you. And do not marry (believing women) to polytheist men until they believe. A believing slave is better than a polytheist man, even if he pleases you. Those call to the Fire. Allah, however, calls to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission, and He makes clear His verses to people, so that they may take heed.
2:222: They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harm. So keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they become clean. When they have cleansed themselves, approach them from where Allah has commanded you. Surely Allah loves those who repent much and loves those who purify themselves much.
2:223: Your women are a tilth for you; come to your tilth however you will, and send forth for yourselves, and fear Allah, and know that you will surely meet Him; and give good tidings to the believers.
2:224: Do not make Allah a target for your oaths against doing good, being mindful, and making peace between people; Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
2:225: Allah does not hold you accountable for idle talk in your oaths, but He holds you accountable for what your hearts have earned.
2:226: For those who swear to abstain from their women, there is a waiting period of four months; then if they turn back, surely Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
2:227: And if they resolve on divorce, surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
2:228: Divorced women shall wait by themselves for three menstrual periods. And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands have more right to take them back during that, if they desire reconciliation. And women have rights similar to the rights over them, according to custom. And men have a degree over them. And Allah is al-Aziz, al-Hakim.
2:229: Divorce is twice. Then either retaining in good manner or releasing with kindness. And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, except if both fear that they cannot uphold the limits of Allah. If you fear that both of them cannot uphold the limits of Allah, then there is no blame on either of them in what the woman ransoms herself with. These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. Whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, then those are the wrongdoers.
2:230: If he divorces her, she is no longer lawful to him after that until she marries another spouse. If he too divorces her, there is no sin upon the two of them if they believe they will maintain the limits of Allah. And these are the limits of Allah; He explains them to a people who know.
2:231: When you divorce women and they reach their term, retain them in good manner or release them in good manner. And do not retain them to harm them, (for then) you will have transgressed the limit. Whoever does that has wronged himself. Do not take the verses of Allah in jest. Remember the favor of Allah upon you, and what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom; He admonishes you with it. Fear Allah, and know that Allah is Knower of all things.
2:232: When you divorce women and they have reached their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they agree between themselves in a proper manner. With this is admonished whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day. That is cleaner and purer for you. Allah knows, and you do not know.
2:233: Mothers suckle their children for two full years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing. And upon the father (falls) their provision and their clothing in kindness. No soul is burdened beyond its capacity. Let not a mother be harmed on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child. And upon the heir is the same (burden). If they (the parents) desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation between them, there is no sin upon them. If you wish to have your children nursed (by a wet nurse), there is no sin upon you as long as you hand over what you give in kindness. Fear Allah and know that Allah is the Seer of what you do.
2:234: Those of you who die and leave wives behind, their wives shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days; when their term is fulfilled, there is no sin upon you in what they do concerning themselves in an acceptable manner, and Allah is aware of what you do.
2:235: There is no sin upon you in hinting your proposal of marriage to women or in concealing it within yourselves. Allah knows that you will mention them. But do not make a secret promise with them, except that you speak a recognized word. And do not resolve on the knot of marriage until the prescribed term reaches its end. Know that Allah knows what is within you, so fear Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.
2:236: There is no sin upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them an obligation. Provide for them in an acceptable manner, the wealthy according to his capacity and the poor according to his capacity; this is a duty upon those who do good.
2:237: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have specified for them an obligation, then half of what you have specified is theirs, except if the women forgo it or he in whose hand is the knot of marriage forgoes it. And that you forgo is closer to righteousness (taqwa). Do not forget goodness between you. Indeed, Allah is the Seer of what you do.
2:238: Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient.
2:239: If you fear, then (pray) on foot or riding. But when you are secure, remember Allah as He taught you what you did not know.
2:240: Those of you who die and leave wives behind should make a bequest for their wives of maintenance for a year without expulsion. If they leave of their own accord, there is no sin upon you for what they do concerning themselves in an acceptable manner. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
2:241: And for divorced women, a provision according to what is acceptable is a duty upon the righteous.
2:242: Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses so that you may reason.
2:243: Did you not see those who went forth from their homes—and they were thousands—in fear of death? Allah said to them, 'Die!' Then He brought them back to life. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty towards people, but most of the people do not give thanks.
2:244: Fight in the cause of Allah, and know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
2:245: Whoever lends Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for him many times over. Allah withholds and extends, and to Him you will be returned.
2:246: Did you not see the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses? When they said to their prophet, 'Send us a king so that we may fight in the cause of Allah.' He said, 'Could it be that if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight?' They said, 'What is the matter with us that we should not fight in the cause of Allah, when we have been driven out from our homes and our children?' But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except a few of them. Allah knows the wrongdoers.
2:247: Their prophet said to them, 'Indeed, Allah has sent Talut to you as king.' They said, 'How can he have kingship over us when we are more worthy of kingship than he, and he has not been given an abundance of wealth?' He said, 'Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him abundantly in knowledge and physique.' Allah gives His kingdom to whom He wills. Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
2:248: Their prophet said to them, 'The sign of his kingship is that there will come to you the ark in which is reassurance from your Rabb and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, carried by the angels.' Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.
2:249: When Talut set out with the armies, he said, 'Indeed, Allah will test you with a river. Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is of me, except whoever takes a handful with his hand.' But they drank from it, except a very few of them. When he and those who believed with him crossed it, they said, 'Today we have no power against Jalut and his armies.' Those who thought that they would meet Allah said, 'How many a small company has overcome a large company by Allah's permission!' Allah is with the patient.
2:250: When they came forth against Jalut and his army, they said, 'Our Rabb, pour out patience upon us, make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people.'
2:251: Thereupon, by Allah's permission, they routed them, and David killed Jalut, and Allah gave him kingship and wisdom and taught him from what He willed. And were it not for Allah repelling people, some by means of others, the earth would surely be corrupted. But Allah is full of bounty towards the worlds.
2:252: These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth. Indeed, you are of those sent.
2:253: Those messengers—We favored some of them over others. Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised the degrees of some. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus). If Allah had willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them. But they differed; some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. If Allah had willed, they would not have fought. But Allah does whatever He wills.
2:254: O you who believe, spend from what We have provided you before a Day comes in which there is neither trading, nor friendship, nor intercession.
2:255: Allah—there is no deity except Him. He is al-Hayy (the Ever-Living), al-Qayyum (the Sustainer of all). Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him alone belongs (everything) that is in the heavens and that is in the earth. Who is it that can intercede in His presence except with His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them. And they cannot encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth. And preserving and guarding the two does not burden Him. And He is al-Aliyy (the Most High), al-Azim (the Most Great).
2:256: There is no compulsion in religion. Right guidance has become distinct from error. So whoever disbelieves in taghut and believes in Allah has certainly grasped the firm handhold that does not break. Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
2:257: Allah is the ally of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into the light. As for those who disbelieve, their allies are taghut; they bring them out from the light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the fire; they will abide eternally therein.
2:258: Did you not see the one who argued with Abraham about his Rabb because Allah had given him kingship? When Abraham said: 'My Rabb is the One Who gives life and causes death.' He said: 'I give life and cause death.' Abraham said: 'Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.' Thereupon the one who disbelieved was dumbfounded. Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
2:259: Or like the one who passed by a village fallen upon its trellises. He said: 'How will Allah bring this to life after its death?' Thereupon Allah caused him to remain dead for a hundred years, then He resurrected him. He said: 'How long did you remain?' He said: 'I remained a day or part of a day.' He said: 'No, you have remained a hundred years. Look at your food and your drink, it has not spoiled. Look at your donkey as well. And that We may make you a sign for the people. Look at the bones, how We raise them up, then clothe them with flesh.' When it became clearly evident to him, he said: 'I know that indeed Allah has power over all things.'
2:260: When Abraham said: 'My Rabb, show me how You give life to the dead.' He said: 'Do you not believe?' He said: 'Yes, but so that my heart may be at peace.' He said: 'Then take four birds, incline them to yourself, then place a part of them upon every mountain, then call them; they will come to you running. Know that Allah is al-Aziz, al-Hakim.'
2:261: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain of seed that brings forth seven ears; in each ear there are a hundred grains of seed, and Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, Knowing.
2:262: Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and then do not follow what they spent with reminders of generosity or hurt, their reward is with their Rabb.
2:263: A kind word and forgiveness is better than a charity followed by hurt. Allah is Self-Sufficient, Forbearing.
2:264: O you who believe, do not invalidate your charities with reminders of generosity and hurt, like the one who spends his wealth to show off to the people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like the example of a smooth rock on which is soil; a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare. They have no power over anything of what they have earned. Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
2:265: The example of those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of Allah and out of a strengthening from their souls is like the example of a garden situated on a hill; heavy rain strikes it, so it yields its fruit twofold; if heavy rain does not strike it, then a drizzle (is sufficient). Allah sees what you do.
2:266: Would any of you wish to have a garden of date palms and grapevines underneath which rivers flow, having in it every kind of fruit, and old age has reached him and he has weak children, whereupon a fiery whirlwind strikes it and it burns?
2:267: O you who believe, spend from the good things of what you have earned and from what We have brought forth for you from the earth. Do not aim at what is bad to spend (from it), while you would not take it except by closing your eyes. And know that Allah is Rich, Praiseworthy.
2:268: Satan promises you poverty and commands you to indecency, while Allah promises you forgiveness and bounty from Himself, and Allah is All-Encompassing, Knowing.
2:269: He grants wisdom to whom He wills. And whoever is granted wisdom has indeed been granted much good. And none take heed except the people of understanding.
2:270: Whatever expenditure you spend or whatever vow you make, Allah surely knows it, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.
2:271: If you give charities openly, how excellent that is. If you conceal them and give them to the poor, that is better for you, and it pardons some of your sins. Allah is well-acquainted with what you do.
2:272: Their guidance is not upon you, but Allah guides whom He wills. Whatever good you spend is for your own souls. And you do not spend except seeking the face of Allah. Whatever good you spend will be paid back to you in full, and you will not be wronged.
2:273: (It is) for the poor who are constrained in the way of Allah, unable to travel about the earth. The unaware thinks them rich because of their restraint. You recognize them by their features; they do not ask from people insistently. Whatever good you spend, indeed Allah knows it.
2:274: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly, their reward is with their Rabb, and there is no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
2:275: Those who consume interest do not stand except as one stands whom Satan has struck. That is because of their saying: 'Trade is also like interest.' Allah has made trade lawful and made interest unlawful. So whoever receives an admonition from his Rabb and desists, what is past is his, and his affair belongs to Allah. And whoever returns, those are the companions of the fire; they will abide therein eternally.
2:276: Allah destroys interest and increases charities. Allah does not love any ungrateful sinner.
2:277: Indeed, those who believe, do righteous deeds, establish salah and give zakat, their reward is with their Rabb, there is no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
2:278: O you who believe, beware of Allah and leave what remains of interest, if you are believers.
2:279: If you do not, then know of a war (declared) by Allah and His Messenger. If you repent, your principal capital is yours; you will neither do wrong nor be wronged.
2:280: And if he is one of hardship, then respite (is granted) until ease. And that you give charity is better for you, if you know.
2:281: Beware of the Day in which you will be returned to Allah, then every soul will be paid in full what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.
2:282: O you who believe, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. Let a scribe write between you with justice. Let not the scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him; let him write. And let the one who is indebted dictate, let him fear Allah, his Rabb, and not diminish anything from it. If the debtor is foolish or weak or unable to dictate himself, let his guardian dictate with justice. Take two witnesses from your men. If there are not two men, then a man and two women from the witnesses whom you approve of, so that if one of them forgets, the other may remind her. Let not the witnesses refuse when they are called. Do not be weary of writing the debt, whether small or large, until its term. This is more just in the sight of Allah, firmer for testimony, and more suitable that you do not doubt. Except if it is an immediate commerce that you conduct among yourselves, there is no sin upon you in not writing it down. Take witnesses when you trade. Let no harm be done to the scribe or to the witness. If you do (harm), this is indeed a transgression for you. Fear Allah; Allah teaches you. Allah knows all things.
2:283: If you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then there are pledges taken. If some of you trust one another, then let the one who is trusted pay back his trust and let him fear Allah, his Rabb. Do not conceal testimony. Whoever conceals it, indeed his heart is sinful. Allah is Knower of what you do.
2:284: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth belongs to Allah. Whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. Allah is capable of all things.
2:285: The Messenger believed in what was sent down to him from his Rabb, and so did the believers. All of them believed in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. They said: 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers.' 'We have heard and we have obeyed. We seek Your forgiveness, our Rabb, and to You is the return.'
2:286: Allah does not burden any soul with other than what it can bear. What it has earned is in its favor, and what it has taken upon itself is against it. Our Rabb, do not hold us responsible if we forget or make a mistake. Our Rabb, do not place a heavy burden upon us as You placed upon those before us. Our Rabb, do not burden us with what we have no power to bear; pardon us, forgive us, have mercy on us. You are our Mawla, help us against the disbelieving people.
